search.description: Keywords within this object only, matched by Postgres full-text search over its label and searchable fields. Every word must match, as a whole word or the start of one ("Dan" finds "Dana"); accents are ignored.

groupBy.description: A filterable select field: also compute the total and aggregates per option.

from.description: The event type the events have now (API name), e.g. "meeting".

to.description: The event type they move to (API name), e.g. "conversation".

events.description: Only these events, all of type from (at most 1000). Without it, every live event of from moves.

fields.description: Source field name to target field name, for fields named differently, e.g. { "agenda": "topic" }. Other fields map by name; title and summary always map to the target's own.

drop.description: Source fields whose values you agree to delete because the target has no field for them. Without it, a move that would lose values is refused with the list.

defaults.description: Target field values for moved events that have no value for that field, written as if logged with the event, e.g. { "medium": "meeting" } when moving meetings to conversation.

dryRun.description: Check the move and report what it would do, changing nothing.

search.description: Keywords within this object only, matched by Postgres full-text search over its label and searchable fields. Every word must match, as a whole word or the start of one ("Dan" finds "Dana"); accents are ignored.

filter.description: Filter by a shared event column or by type. The type filter supports eq, neq, and in.

linked.description: Event types only: events directly attached to this record, as a participant, about it, or through one of the event's own relation fields (link: field).

search.description: Keywords within this object only, matched by Postgres full-text search over its label and searchable fields. Every word must match, as a whole word or the start of one ("Dan" finds "Dana"); accents are ignored.

linked.description: Event types only: events directly attached to this record, as a participant, about it, or through one of the event's own relation fields (link: field).

object.description: Singular API name of the object, e.g. "person", as describe_schema lists it.

values.description: Field name to value, in its type's format from describe_schema's valueFormats. Composite fields (emails, phones, links, money, full_name, address) are replaced whole, so include the values to keep. null clears a field. A many_to_many relation takes the whole list of record IDs ([] clears it): read the record first and send every member to keep. Fields marked readOnly are not yours to write: an inverse relation (isInverse) is written from the other side, and any other is written only by the app that added it.

ifMissing.description: When id or match finds nothing: "fail" (default) or "create". Use "create" only when you mean to add a new record.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: Reject the write if the record changed since this updatedAt.

source.description: The event id (from log_event) these values come from. Values then carry the event's date, so an older email cannot overwrite a newer claim. Omit only for values that come from no conversation.

idempotencyKey.description: Only for creates without id or match: retrying with the same key returns the first result instead of creating a second record.
